projects.title: HappyFone WebUI
projects.tagline: The working prototype of the HappyPhone caller softphone.
projects.summary: A dependency-free agent console for the HappyPhone callers: sign-in, a live agent state machine, T9 dialing, a simulated call lifecycle, and persistent call history.

sections.title: What it is
body: HappyFone WebUI is the prototype of the softphone I'm building for HappyPhone. It is a production-style agent console with no framework and no dependencies — plain HTML, CSS and ES modules, deployed on GitHub Pages.
The point was to make the caller's day concrete before wiring real telephony: where they sign in, how they go available, what happens between calls, and what they see when one ends.

sections.title: What's inside
bullets: Mock auth and a session guard: username, extension, password; direct dashboard visits bounce back to sign-in
Agent state machine — AVAILABLE, ON_CALL, WRAP_UP, AUX — with a live timer
AUX reasons (lunch, short break, bio, coaching, training) that pause the dialer until the agent returns
Simulated call lifecycle: ringing, connected timer, mute, hold/resume and hangup
Keyboard-first dialing, including T9 letter mapping and DTMF tones while connected
A five-second wrap-up countdown, then back to available
Persistent call history that survives reloads, with click-to-dial
Responsive dark UI with accessible focus states and reduced-motion support

sections.title: What is still simulated
body: Auth is mocked and calls are simulated — there is no real audio path yet. The production softphone is the one I'm building at happyphone.lol/caller: real JWT auth, a Kamailio + RTPEngine gateway, and calls through the team's VoIP.ms sub-account.

projects.title: AI Voice Receptionist
projects.tagline: Answer every missed and after-hours call. Book the slot. Alert your team.
projects.summary: Answers missed and after-hours calls for appointment-based businesses, captures structured intake, books appointments and logs every conversation — built three times (Make, n8n, Zapier) over one shared Retell voice layer.

sections.title: Overview
body: A phone is a business's front door. When nobody picks up — lunch, after hours, a busy morning — the caller either leaves a vague voicemail or calls the next business on their list. Salons, clinics, med spas, trades — the pattern is the same.
This is an AI receptionist that picks up instead: it captures structured intake, checks the calendar, books a real slot, logs the call and alerts your team with a summary.

sections.title: What it does
bullets: Answers missed and after-hours calls, 24/7
Captures caller intake as structured data (not a transcript to re-read)
Conflict-checks Google Calendar and books a real slot
Alerts your team with a short summary
Logs every call to Google Sheets
Configurable services, hours, intake fields and escalation

sections.title: How it's built
body: One shared voice layer on Retell, three interchangeable engines. The same receptionist is implemented on Make, n8n and Zapier so a business can keep the stack it already pays for instead of adopting a new one.

The n8n branch runs end to end on synthetic call payloads — real Google Calendar booking, Sheets logging and Gmail alerts. The phone call itself is simulated; live telephony is a documented Retell setup away. Make and Zapier remain simulated.

sections.title: Compliance
body: A HIPAA-compliant build is available for practices that will handle real patient information: scoped architecture, BAAs, access controls, audit logging, a PHI-safe infrastructure and vendor review before go-live. Compliance is established per deployment, not claimed by the public demo.

use_cases.title: After-hours intake
use_cases.body: Answer the calls that arrive after your team closes, capture the reason for the call, and book the next open slot.

use_cases.title: Lunch and overflow
use_cases.body: Pick up the calls a busy team cannot reach, so a ringing phone never becomes a lost customer.

use_cases.title: New-customer screening
use_cases.body: Collect contact details, the service needed and the reason for the call before a human touches the schedule.

use_cases.title: Cancellation recovery
use_cases.body: Offer freed slots to callers instead of letting them fall into voicemail.

projects.title: Sales Call QA & Coaching
projects.tagline: Score every sales call against the same rubric — and only bother a manager when the evidence is thin.
projects.summary: Scores every sales call against your script, verifies each quoted claim against the transcript, gates low-confidence scores for human review, and emails a weekly coaching digest.

sections.title: Overview
body: Sales calls are the revenue engine, but managers only hear the one call they happened to sit in on. Coaching runs on memory, and the same objection gets mishandled in three different ways.

This workflow scores every call against the same five-part rubric, quotes the exact line behind each score, and routes only the calls that need a human — low confidence, a red flag, or a compliance miss. Everything else lands in a data table and a Monday digest.

sections.title: How it works
bullets: Retell posts the finished call to a webhook; a form accepts a pasted transcript for testing
A Code node normalizes the payload and refuses to score a call without a usable transcript
Gemini scores opening, discovery, objection handling, next step and compliance through a structured output parser
A second Code node clamps the scores, recomputes the weighted overall, verifies each quote against the transcript, and redacts emails and phone numbers
Clean calls go to the Sales Call QA data table; risky or low-confidence calls also become a Gmail draft for a manager
Every Monday, a digest aggregates the last week per rep and files one coaching draft

sections.title: Guardrails
bullets: Every score must cite an exact quote; unverifiable evidence lowers confidence and forces review
The overall is computed in code, not guessed by the model
Any red flag, compliance below 3, or confidence below 0.75 always needs a human
No objection? Objection handling scores 3 with “no objection in transcript” — the rep is not punished for an easy call
Nothing is sent automatically — Gmail drafts wait for a manager
Transcripts are truncated, and emails and phone numbers are redacted in the stored evidence

sections.title: Honest limits
body: The demo runs on synthetic calls. The Retell webhook is wired, but live telephony needs a real Retell agent and a public n8n URL. On the demo instance the Gmail credential was expired during the build, so draft creation is skipped while the scorecard still saves — reconnect it to see the manager drafts.

use_cases.title: New-hire onboarding
use_cases.body: Baseline a new SDR in week one and track opening, discovery, objection handling, next step and compliance as they improve.

use_cases.title: Weekly rep coaching
use_cases.body: Give every rep a scorecard with exact quotes instead of a manager’s memory of one call.

use_cases.title: Objection library
use_cases.body: Find the objections that get dismissed and turn the best responses into a shared playbook.

use_cases.title: Next-step discipline
use_cases.body: Catch calls that end with “I’ll follow up sometime” and coach the date-and-owner habit.

use_cases.title: AI SDR QA
use_cases.body: Score the AI SDR with the same rubric as the humans, so the comparison is honest.

use_cases.title: Compliance review
use_cases.body: Check recording disclosure, pricing claims and do-not-call handling across the team.

projects.title: AR Invoice Reminder
projects.tagline: A daily n8n agent that chases overdue invoices — and never sends anything itself.
projects.summary: Finds overdue invoices in your tracker, computes days past due, drafts a tone-matched reminder, and files it as a Gmail draft — a human approves; nothing sends itself.

sections.title: Overview
body: Chasing overdue invoices is the work nobody schedules. It is not hard — it is just always later, until a receivable is 90 days old and the polite reminder you meant to send in week two would now read like an apology for your own silence.
This is a daily n8n workflow that reads the invoice tracker, works out how late each invoice is, and drafts a reminder whose tone matches the delay.

sections.title: How it works
bullets: Schedule trigger fires at 09:00 and reads the invoice sheet
A Code node drops paid and void rows, parses amounts and dates, computes days past due and picks a tone
Gemini drafts against a structured output parser
A second Code node enforces the signature and falls back to a template if the model returns nothing usable
The draft lands in Gmail — nobody sends an email automatically
The follow-up date is written back to the sheet

sections.title: Guardrails
bullets: Tone is computed in code, not guessed: friendly under 14 days, firm to 30, solution-oriented after
The signature is rebuilt in code, so the model can't rewrite it
A 7-day cooldown per invoice stops duplicate chasing
Strict JSON, no placeholders, a human presses send

use_cases.title: Net-30 and net-60 clients
use_cases.body: Sweep the tracker daily and match the reminder tone to how late the invoice actually is.

use_cases.title: Retainer and milestone billing
use_cases.body: Chase the invoice without sounding like you are chasing the relationship.

use_cases.title: Disputed invoices
use_cases.body: Stop the sequence when a client replies with a question and escalate with the full context.

use_cases.title: Owner approval
use_cases.body: Every reminder waits as a Gmail draft; nobody sends a collections email by accident.

projects.title: Dead Lead Retrieval
projects.tagline: Dormant leads rarely die because someone said no. They die because nobody followed up.
projects.summary: Finds stale leads, drafts a personalized check-in with an LLM, files it as a Gmail draft, and tracks every lead in your CRM until someone replies.

sections.title: Overview
body: A dormant list is not a dead list. Most of it is people who got busy, changed priorities, or never got a second reply — and manual follow-up is the first thing to slip when the week gets loud.
This pipeline resurrects those leads with personalized check-in emails that a human approves, and keeps the status honest in your CRM.

sections.title: The loop
bullets: Pull the dormant leads and their original context
An LLM drafts a short, specific check-in — never a generic blast
The email is filed as a Gmail draft for review
A booking link is added so a reply turns into a call
CRM tracks each lead through the review lifecycle

sections.title: Guardrails
bullets: AI drafts, a human approves — nothing sends itself
Anti-hallucination rules: the only link in any email is mine
Original context is passed to the model so the note is relevant
Every action is visible in the CRM, not buried in a mailbox

use_cases.title: Dormant CRM
use_cases.body: Reopen old leads with a specific note that references the original conversation, not a blast.

use_cases.title: Quote follow-up
use_cases.body: Follow up on estimates that never got a yes or a no, before they go cold.

use_cases.title: Event and webinar lists
use_cases.body: Turn a tired attendee list into real conversations with a human approving every send.

use_cases.title: Trial expiry
use_cases.body: Check in before a trial quietly lapses, with the original context already in the draft.

projects.title: job-scrapper
projects.tagline: A Python scraper that watches OnlineJobs.ph and posts one Discord embed per job.
projects.summary: Reads configurable job categories every four hours, summarizes each listing with Gemini, and posts only new roles to Discord — deduped by URL. Migrating from a single GitHub Actions run to an n8n workflow.
projects.status: Live · every 4 hours · n8n migration in progress

gallery.alt: Pipeline history: the Make.com era (retired), the current GitHub Actions run, and the n8n migration in progress
The v1 Make.com scenario: webhook to router to Telegram Bot, with Gemini and HTTP nodes
Planned n8n canvas: webhook, split out, dedupe against the seen table, Gemini summary, Discord embed, respond 200 or 502

sections.title: Overview
body: Job boards reward the first reply. A scraper that checks every ten minutes gets blocked; one that checks once a day is too late.
job-scrapper searches OnlineJobs.ph on a four-hour cadence, keeps the freshest listing per keyword, and posts one rich Discord embed per job so the channel stays readable.

sections.title: How it works
bullets: Searches each category's keywords with a randomized 5–12 second pause between requests
Parses every result card and sorts by the exact posting timestamp
Keeps the top listing per keyword, dedupes across keywords, caps per category
Visits each listing for the full description and splits out the "How to Apply" section
Summarizes each job with Gemini (falling back to raw fields if the API fails)
Dedupes by URL through seen_jobs.json so repeat runs stay quiet

sections.title: Pipeline history
bullets: v1 · Make.com (retired): GitHub Actions POSTed each job as JSON to a Make webhook; the scenario routed it through Gemini and delivered to Telegram
v2 · GitHub Actions (current): scrape, Gemini summary and Discord delivery all run in one workflow, deduped by seen_jobs.json
v3 · n8n (on hold): GitHub Actions posts a batch to an n8n webhook; n8n owns the job_scrapper_seen dedupe table, the Gemini summary and the Discord post. Saved and waiting on the new n8n version

sections.title: Notes
body: It started as a Make.com webhook pipeline with Telegram delivery, then moved fully into GitHub Actions: scrape, summarize, post — no second platform in the loop.

The next step is an n8n workflow: GitHub Actions keeps the cron and the polite scraping, then posts a batch to an n8n webhook that owns dedupe state, the Gemini summary and the Discord delivery. The workflow is written and on hold until the new n8n version lands.

use_cases.title: Job seekers
use_cases.body: Get fresh listings in Discord before the board fills with applicants.

use_cases.title: Recruiters
use_cases.body: Watch niche categories and keywords without refreshing the site all day.

use_cases.title: Niche boards
use_cases.body: Swap the source and keep the same summarize-and-post pipeline.

use_cases.body: One embed per job, deduped, every four hours, so the channel stays readable.

projects.title: signal-checker
projects.tagline: An SMA crossover pipeline that evaluates daily prices and dispatches signals as JSON.
projects.summary: Pulls ~400 days of daily closes, computes the 50/200-day crossover, and posts one BUY, SELL or HOLD signal to Make every weekday — no dashboard to stare at.

sections.title: Overview
body: A small, deliberately boring signals pipeline: one strategy, one schedule, one JSON payload. It exists to keep the downstream automation fed, not to predict the market.

sections.title: How it works
bullets: Fetches roughly 400 days of daily closes through yfinance (50/200-day defaults)
Computes a simple moving-average crossover and emits BUY, SELL or HOLD
Dispatches the result as JSON to a Make.com webhook
Runs on GitHub Actions every weekday at 21:00 UTC
Configurable through environment variables: symbol, SMA windows, webhook URL
Forex pairs like USD/PHP are normalized automatically to yfinance format

use_cases.title: Personal watchlist
use_cases.body: One symbol, one strategy, one scheduled JSON payload.

use_cases.title: Downstream bots
use_cases.body: Feed Make, n8n or a Telegram bot without scraping a chart.

use_cases.title: Paper trading
use_cases.body: Test a crossover rule before risking money on it.

use_cases.title: Forex and equities
use_cases.body: Normalize symbols like USD/PHP automatically and keep the schedule boring.

gallery.alt: The Weekly News Facebook scenario in Make.com: Webhook to Google Gemini AI to Router to HTTP to Facebook Pages

sections.title: Overview
body: rss-news feeds the AI Tech & Automation Hub page without a human in the loop: Python fetches the week's RSS links on a Sunday cron, filters and dedupes them, and hands a clean digest to Make.com. Gemini writes the post, Imagen generates the graphic, and Facebook Pages publishes it — the only manual step is reading it.

sections.title: Pipeline
bullets: Python fetches Hacker News, Phoronix, The Verge and other RSS feeds
Keyword filtering plus seen_articles.json dedupe so nothing posts twice
The digest is POSTed to a Make.com webhook
Runs on the Make.com free tier — 1,000 operations a month covers a weekly run many times over; the trade-off is the 15-minute webhook polling interval, which doesn't matter on a Sunday cron
Gemini drafts the post, Imagen generates the graphic, Facebook Pages publishes it
GitHub Actions runs the whole thing every Sunday at 06:00 PHT

projects.title: Tippy Card Monte
projects.tagline: Follow the shuffle. Six modes. One very smug coin.
projects.summary: A pixel-art card monte in a single page: six modes including Bet, uncapped streak payouts, checkpoint perks, 15 medals and landscape fullscreen. No build, no backend.

sections.title: Overview
body: Tippy Card Monte is a small pixel card game: a shuffled row, a slightly smug mascot, and a bet that gets harder every round. It is built to be played in a browser tab for five minutes, not installed.

The 1.3.6 update adds Bet mode with infinite rounds, removes the +25p reward cap, expands the medal gallery, and adds an in-game EXIT button. Bet mode uses a 100p bankroll, stakes up to 100p, a cash-out pot and allowed debt; it shows Tippy for the normal peek, then asks you to find him. Exit returns home and forfeits any unbanked pot. Reverse mode is temporarily unavailable while it is reworked.

sections.title: Six modes
bullets: Classic — 16 rounds, seven stages, 3 to 16 cards. Finish above 0p to win.
Bet — infinite 16-card rounds, find Tippy after the peek, stakes up to 100p, a cash-out pot and allowed debt. Exit returns home; unbanked pot is forfeited.
Endless — no fail. Start at 16 cards, climb forever, and cash out when you want to bank your best depth.
Daily — one date-seeded 16-round shuffle per day. Today’s best score is saved.
Blitz — eight fast rounds with 6 to 16 cards. Pure score chase.
Zen — 16 rounds, no fail, no debt pressure, slower peeks.

sections.title: Checkpoints and perks
bullets: Every 4 Endless depths pauses for a 30/40/50…p checkpoint bonus.
Choose one of three random perks: Longer Peek, Fewer Shuffles, Slow Hands, Coin Purse, Safety Net or Streak Guard.
Each perk has three ranks. Safety Net forgives one miss; Streak Guard keeps the streak.
The HUD shows the next checkpoint count and a single-press CASH OUT button; the checkpoint screen has its own CASH OUT button.

sections.title: Medals and bests
bullets: 15 medals persist in localStorage, with unlock toasts and a gallery on the title screen.
Each mode keeps its own best score or best Endless depth.
The result screen reports mode, depth, new medals and the mode best.
Everything runs locally: no accounts, no backend, no network calls.
Fullscreen toggles from the title screen, the HUD, or F; touch devices request landscape and show a rotate prompt if the lock is unavailable.

projects.title: AdBlock Island
projects.tagline: A wholesome micro-RPG in a single HTML file — online co-op with a shared bench wall, server-moderated rooms and host handover.
projects.summary: Pick one of nine classes, sweep the static, and survive the Algorithm. Room-code co-op runs on a token-guarded Vercel room desk — Redis or a connected Blob store — with server-moderated chat, shared bench-wall notes, spectators and host handover.

sections.title: Overview
body: AdBlock Island is a small, wholesome micro-RPG about cleaning up a beach that ads have overrun. You wash ashore with a broom and a class, and the islanders save you a spot by the fire.

It is one self-contained HTML file: no build step, no CDN, no images, no fonts, no accounts, no trackers. The island is drawn with Canvas 2D; the ocean, lo-fi chords and sound effects are synthesized with Web Audio.

The online beta adds room-code co-op on Vercel. A single serverless room service owns rooms, issues peer tokens, relays WebRTC signaling, filters and rate-limits chat, and stores the handover backup. Guests join with a code or invite link, buy their own upgrades, chat through the service, or watch as a spectator; the island hands over to the next hero when the host leaves.

sections.title: What's in the beta
bullets: Nine classes with their own silhouettes, gear, projectiles and hit behaviour
Room-code online co-op for up to four heroes, host-authoritative over WebRTC
A token-guarded Vercel room service: membership, signaling, moderation and handover state
Server-side chat filtering, 2s rate limits, host-enforced mutes and long-poll delivery
Guests move, aim, attack; Q/E skills and dash run on the host with visible cooldowns
A full guest upgrade tree, kettle breaks, guest pause/leave and spectator mode
A shared bench wall: guests read and pin notes on the host's island
Wave banners, guest wave cards and online achievements in every room
Host handover: the island backs itself up and the next hero takes over
Optional TURN relay settings for stubborn NATs
Pop-up ads reach remote heroes: CLICK HERE hurts that hero, the ✕ pays Joy
The wave ladder, Endless mode with checkpoints, medals, items and kindness notes
Two bosses maximum: a 33% spawn roll per eligible wave, one 75% split, +25% speed with both alive
Same-keyboard co-op, plus a committed Playwright test suite
Runs from a static host, from the release zip, or straight from file://

sections.title: Honest limits
body: Vercel functions are HTTP request/response, so this is a room service, not a persistent game server: gameplay stays host-simulated, chat moderation is automated filtering rather than a human process, and handover is best-effort. Dedicated simulation authority and full anti-cheat remain later work.
Versions count from zero while the game is in beta. The online branch restarts the count at 0.1.0; the current online build is v0.7.0 Room service. The stable build remains v0.9.8 on GitHub Pages.
